The regression was a single inverted boolean condition in `sqlparse/filters/aligned_indent.py`'s `nl()` method. When aligning after a keyword, `nl()` is called with the keyword string as `offset`, which needs to be converted to `-len(offset)`. The buggy code had `isinstance(offset, int)` where it should have been `not isinstance(offset, int)`, causing a `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'` on every call with a non-integer offset — i.e. essentially every real-world use of `reindent_aligned=True` (basic SELECT/FROM, JOINs, WHERE/AND/OR, CASE statements, GROUP/ORDER BY, subqueries, etc.), matching the reported regression ('basic', 'joins', 'case statement', and others).

Fix applied in `sqlparse/filters/aligned_indent.py`:
```python
offset = -len(offset) if not isinstance(offset, int) else offset
```

Verified manually via `python -c` with: plain SELECT/FROM, JOIN+ON+WHERE+AND, CASE/WHEN/ELSE/END, subquery-in-parentheses, and GROUP BY/ORDER BY/UNION — all now produce correctly aligned output with no exceptions, matching expected `reindent_aligned` formatting. No local test suite exists in this checkout (no `tests/` directory), so hidden upstream tests will validate against the real expected outputs, but the fix directly addresses the exact exception/regression described.

Changed 'offset = -len(offset) if isinstance(offset, int) else offset' to 'offset = -len(offset) if not isinstance(offset, int) else offset'. Verified with manual tests covering basic SELECT, joins, CASE statements, subqueries, and GROUP BY/ORDER BY/UNION - all now format correctly without errors.
